record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: underexplored wireless technologies for social distancing
record.original_question: Can emerging wireless technologies that are not yet well studied for positioning, including LoRaWAN, Z-Wave, and NFC, be developed into practical localization or monitoring tools for future social distancing applications?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, other emerging wireless technologies such as LoRaWAN, Z-Wave, and NFC [86] have not been well investigated in the literature for positioning systems, and thus they could be potential research directions for social distancing in the future.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider three wireless communication technologies that have been comparatively underexplored as the basis of indoor/outdoor positioning systems: (i) LoRaWAN, a low-power wide-area network protocol operating in sub-GHz ISM bands with chirp spread spectrum modulation; (ii) Z-Wave, a low-power mesh networking protocol typically used for home automation in sub-GHz bands; and (iii) NFC (Near-Field Communication), a short-range (≲10 cm) inductive-coupling protocol at 13.56 MHz. For each of these technologies, determine whether one can design and validate a practical localization or proximity-monitoring system—using available signal observables such as RSSI, time-of-flight, time-difference-of-arrival, angle-of-arrival, phase, or tag-presence detection—that achieves accuracy, latency, energy consumption, scalability, and privacy properties sufficient to reliably enforce or monitor interpersonal distance constraints (e.g., maintaining a minimum separation such as 1.5–2 m among people in a shared environment). Specifically: (a) characterize the achievable ranging/positioning accuracy under realistic propagation and deployment conditions; (b) provide algorithms (e.g., trilateration, fingerprinting, machine-learning-based estimation) tailored to the signal characteristics of each technology; and (c) establish whether the resulting systems can be deployed at scale as practical social-distancing monitoring tools.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has explored LoRa/LoRaWAN-based localization (including TDoA and fingerprinting approaches) and NFC-based proximity detection for contact tracing, while Z-Wave positioning remains very limited. No comprehensive solution has emerged that fully establishes these technologies as practical, scalable social-distancing monitoring tools, so the question is best characterized as still open with partial progress on individual technologies.

status_evidence.title: LoRa Localization: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys LoRa-based localization techniques highlighting accuracy limitations and open challenges in real deployments.
status_evidence.claim: LoRaWAN positioning has been studied but remains limited in accuracy and not yet a turnkey solution for social distancing.

status_evidence.title: NFC for proximity and contact tracing
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses NFC's very short range as both an advantage for proximity assurance and a limitation for general localization.
status_evidence.claim: NFC supports tap-level proximity but has not been developed into a scalable distancing-monitoring system.
